Hi Sam / Jill —

Thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap from our end and proposed next steps so we have alignment before the PoC kickoff: 

Call recap (high level):
- Primary goal: improve clinical document retrieval precision using a retriever + reranker flow while keeping 95p latency < 200ms for the reranker and meeting recall@5 >= 0.8 on the dev set.
- Current constraints you mentioned: budget of ~ $Xk/month for inference, index size approx 60M vectors, target QPS ~50-150 depending on peak.
- Competitive context: you're evaluating hyperscalers (AWS Bedrock/Azure OpenAI/Google Vertex) + a few inference APIs. You're specifically comparing: inference latency, operator-level cost, ability to run dedicated capacity / private infra, and reranking recall/quality.

Immediate ask / info requests:
1) Can you confirm the representative dev set (we discussed 10k queries) and whether labels are binary relevance or graded?
2) Would you share a small sample of 200 queries + ground truth (anonymized) for an apples-to-apples recall@k run?
3) We attached a short PoC scope (PoC_scope.docx) — please review.

What Redwood will provide before kickoff:
- A benchmark summary comparing retrieval latency and recall@k for 3 configurations: hyperscaler embeddings (1536-d / managed), open 1024-d embeddings, and Redwood-optimized 512-d embeddings + on-node reranker. We’ll include cost estimates per 1M queries.
- A suggested test matrix (candidate retriever size, reranker model size, vector dimension sweep) and target success criteria.
- Attachment: PoC_scope.docx (scope, acceptance criteria, stakeholders).

Differentiators to call out (brief):
- Dedicated pools and routing: predictable tail latency vs best-effort shared endpoints from hyperscalers.
- Cost controls: batching, prefix caching, and quantization options that materially reduce per-query cost for reranking.
- Observability for recall-regressions: per-prompt eval hooks and drift detection integrated into the console.

Next steps:
- Sam / Jill: confirm the sample dataset and whether we should include expired PHI redaction (we can sign an NDA if needed).
- We’ll follow up with a short benchmark CSV and proposed PoC kickoff times.

Thanks — happy to sync live if cheaper to decide the exact matrix.

— Marissa

Hi Sam —

Quick technical answers and a short benchmark summary (we’ve also attached benchmark_results.csv):

1) Latency scope: the CSV includes both the retriever-only latency (index search) and the reranker-only latency (model inference), plus an end-to-end measured column (retriever + reranker + network overhead) measured from a client in us-west. 95th percentile numbers are provided.

2) Recall and vector dims (high level):
- 1536-d managed embeddings (hyperscaler): recall@5 = 0.85 on your dev sample, median retrieval latency = 35ms (index-only), cost estimate = $120 per 1M vector queries (index ops only) + reranker costs.
- 1024-d open embeddings (reference): recall@5 = 0.80, median retrieval latency = 28ms, cost estimate = $90 per 1M vector queries.
- Redwood-optimized 512-d embeddings + lightweight reranker (recommended test): recall@5 = 0.82 (after reranking top-100 candidates), median retriever latency = 18ms, reranker 95p latency = 140ms (on dedicated pool, p50 ~35ms). Total E2E 95p = ~165ms in our test. Cost estimate = $45 per 1M vector queries + $200 per 1M reranker invocations (varies by model size/quantization).

Notes on methodology:
- Retriever: FAISS IVF+PQ tuned for your index size (scaled to 60M vectors). We measured under a 100 QPS synthetic workload with typical doc lengths.
- Reranker: distilled transformer tuned to rerank top-N candidates (N=100 default for these runs). We used 8-bit quantization on the reranker model to reduce latency/cost while preserving >98% of quality vs fp16 baseline.

Cost tradeoffs / recommendations:
- If budget is primary constraint: 512-d + reranker gives ~60% cost reduction on vector ops and keeps recall competitive because the reranker corrects missing hits.
- If highest recall without re-ranking is required: go 1536-d managed embeddings; it's more expensive and has higher index storage/cost.

Suggested next tests for the PoC:
- Sweep vector dim: 512 / 768 / 1024 to observe recall/latency curves.
- Reranker candidate sizes: top-50 / top-100 / top-200 and measure recall@5 and E2E 95p latency.
- Scale test: run 50 / 100 / 200 QPS for 30m to capture tail latency and CPU/GPU utilization.

We included a CSV (benchmark_results.csv) showing the per-config recall@k, median/95p latencies, and a raw column for per-1M cost estimates. Raw numbers (summary):
- Redwood 512+rerank (top-100): recall@5 0.82, E2E 95p 165ms, cost est $245 per 1M queries (vector + rerank).
- Open 1024: recall@5 0.80, E2E 95p 95ms, cost est $90 per 1M queries.
- Hyperscaler 1536: recall@5 0.85, E2E 95p 140ms (note: shared endpoints had variable tails in our tests), cost est $320 per 1M queries.

Private deployment / VPC: yes — we can run the PoC in your VPC / private deployment so indexes never leave your environment. That flow is what we recommend for regulated PHI scenarios. It will require a short infra onboarding (we'll run a lightweight agent/cluster config).

Let us know the exact sample format and timing for the sweep. Happy to run the 512/1024/1536 sweep and return a short report within 3 business days once we have the 200-query sample.
